LESSON: READING 5.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: FICTION AND NON FICTION MATERIALS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.2: Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials, part of Strand 5 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: where they meet regularly, • share reflections on the books read collaboratively. 1. What materials do you enjoy reading?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work jointly to select texts from a collection,

2. preview a text to determine suitability.

3. scan a text to pick out vocabulary words,

4. skim through reading materials for the main idea,

5. select fiction and non-fiction reading materials of between 1000-1250 words (both print and non-print),

6. read selected materials independently,

7. set up an after-school reading club

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly to select texts from a collection,
2. preview a text to determine suitability.
3. scan a text to pick out vocabulary words,
4. skim through reading materials for the main idea,
5. select fiction and non-fiction reading materials of between 1000-1250 words (both print and non-print),
6. read selected materials independently,
7. set up an after-school reading club

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration is enhanced as the learner sets up an after-school reading club where they meet

regularly with peers to read.

• Digital Literacy is attained as the learner sources for a variety of reading materials online.

• Learning to Learn is developed as the learner engages in independent reading which enhances sourcing for

information and lifetime learning.

Values:
Unity is developed as the learner respects self and others’ opinions when selecting and reading fiction and nonfiction

materials collaboratively.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social justice is enhanced as the learner practises living together through establishment of an after-school reading club.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies extensive reading in other learning areas like Kiswahili which emphasises on the same concept.
